title: Phục hồi hay giam giữ · Agree / Disagree
prompt: Some people believe that using community-based rehabilitation for more non-violent offenders should be a priority. To what extent do you agree or disagree?
instructions: Give reasons for your answer and include any relevant examples from your own knowledge or experience. Write at least 250 words.

paragraphs: Community rehabilitation changes the setting of punishment while retaining obligations intended to prevent further offending. I support extending community rehabilitation to suitable non-violent offenders, provided individual risk assessment, treatment capacity and enforceable supervision protect victims as well as support rehabilitation.

Community sentences can address factors linked to repeated offending without unnecessary imprisonment. Supervised work and treatment can preserve employment and family connections that support lawful routines. An offender with an addiction could receive monitored treatment alongside a meaningful community obligation. Remaining employed may preserve lawful income and routine, while monitored treatment addresses a factor that imprisonment alone may leave unchanged or even aggravate.

Weak supervision can undermine public confidence and fail to protect victims. Without staff and treatment capacity, a community order may exist mainly on paper. Failure to monitor compliance or respond to breaches can leave victims exposed and undermine trust, while the offender receives neither the support nor the credible boundaries needed for rehabilitation. Eligibility should reflect individual risk and programmes should have enforceable conditions. Programme capacity and enforceable conditions are essential, with individual risk assessment preventing a broad offence label from replacing attention to victims and future harm. Supervisors need manageable caseloads and a clear route for reporting breaches, because imposing more conditions cannot improve victim protection if nobody has the time or authority to check compliance. Preserving employment while treating addiction can address recurring causes of crime more directly than imprisonment, but this advantage disappears when monitoring is too weak to protect victims or enforce obligations.

In conclusion, community rehabilitation can produce wider gains than unnecessary custody for suitable offenders, but those gains depend on credible supervision and treatment rather than leniency in name alone.

paragraphs.quote: Weak supervision can undermine public confidence and fail to protect victims. Without staff and treatment capacity, a community order may exist mainly on paper. Eligibility should reflect individual risk and programmes should have enforceable conditions. Programme capacity and enforceable conditions are essential, with individual risk assessment preventing a broad offence label from replacing attention to victims and future harm. Supervisors need manageable caseloads and a clear route for reporting breaches, because imposing more conditions cannot improve victim protection if nobody has the time or authority to check compliance.
